options.help: Language file in plugins/Headcount/lang/ (without .yml).
How dates are written in messages (Java DateTimeFormatter pattern). Shown in the cycle time zone.
How many units a duration shows, e.g. 2 -> "3d 4h", 3 -> "3d 4h 12m". Unit names are in the lang file.
SQLite database file inside plugins/Headcount/. Every change is saved as it happens.
Cycle
Length of a cycle in days. A change applies from the next cycle, or a /hca reset cycle (the running cycle keeps its end).
The day the first cycle starts, as YYYY-MM-DD, or "auto" to start immediately (aligned to end-time today). Before a configured future date, Headcount waits and no cycle runs.
Exact time of day (24h HH:MM) cycles roll over.

Time zone for start-date and end-time. Any of: a region (America/Denver, Europe/London; follows daylight saving), an abbreviation (MST, EST, CET, ...; a fixed offset all year: MST is always UTC-7), an offset (GMT-7, UTC+5:30), or "system". (If the server was offline at a rollover, the next start ends the stored cycle and starts whichever cycle should be running now. Cycle numbers go up by exactly one at each end; /hca reset cycle keeps the number and /hca reset hard starts again at 1. Each run of a cycle also has an internal run ID, shown in /hca cycle info.)
Playtime during a cycle needed to count as active. 0 means joining once is enough. Only active players get a score, points and outcomes.
How often playtime is saved and the active threshold checked.
Head vault (/hc)
Slots in each vault. Up to 54 fits one screen; more than 54 is split into pages of 45. Size and starting heads only change at the start of the next cycle (or at a /hca reset cycle).

Heads of their own every player starts each cycle with (capped at the vault size). Extra starting heads from next-cycle actions (a shop purchase, the streak bonus) that don't fit are given as items instead.
Largest size actions (next-cycle vault-size) may grow a vault to.

Statuses (statuses.yml) that stop a player moving heads in or out of their vault. Each has its own message (lang: gates.vault-move.<status>) and bypass permission (headcount.bypass.vault-move.<status>). Prefix a status with ! to block when it is NOT active.
true: the same statuses also stop the vault from opening at all (messages: gates.vault-open.<status>, bypass: headcount.bypass.vault-open.<status>). false: blocked players can still open and look.

Resets (/hca reset cycle, /hca reset hard)

Every head made before a reset is worthless (it can't go in a vault and never counts). Each reset chooses what happens to them: add delete-heads or keep-heads to the command, or leave it out to use this default. delete (true): deleted wherever Headcount sees them: inventories and ender chests at the reset and on join, containers when opened, items picked up or dropped (a broken placed head), queued deliveries. keep (false):  they stay as defunct heads (heads.item.defunct-name and defunct-lore). The choice is stored with each reset, so changing this later doesn't change what earlier resets did.
/hca reset hard deletes every player's Headcount data and starts again from cycle 1, keeping these config files. It needs the headcount.admin.reset.hard permission (the console always has it).

Hooks: action lists that run at moments in the cycle and in a player's time on the server. Every list uses the actions system (see actions.yml for every type and the common options). Cycle hooks (cycle-start, cycle-end, and each warning) have (cycle-start also runs after /hca reset cycle): global:      runs once for the server, with cycle-wide variables per-player:  runs once for each player with their own variables players:   all | active | inactive | online offline:   deliver (store it and run it on their next join) | skip expire-after-cycles: a stored hook older than this many cycles is dropped actions:   the list Global variables: <cycle> <cycle_start> <cycle_end> <time_left> <cycle_length> <active> <players> cycle-end adds: <average_score> <rewarded> <punished> <top_list> <top_N_name> <top_N_unique> <top_N_score> Per-player variables at cycle-end: <player> <unique> <total> <own> <score> <rank> <percentile> <streak> <streak_text> <points_earned> <points> <rolled_over> <tier> <outcomes> <playtime> <kills> <deaths> <trades> Player hooks (player:) run per player. When several run on one join the order is: delivered per-player cycle hooks, first-join, first-join-cycle, became-active, join. ---- PvPManager (provider: pvpmanager) ----

PvPManager only lets players use /pvp with its permission pvpmanager.command.pvp, which is off by default, and players start with PvP on. Headcount's default rules block moving heads and trading while PvP is on, so with this on, every player may use /pvp (the permission's default becomes true; a player or group that is explicitly denied it in your permissions plugin stays denied). Set false to hand the permission out yourself.
Placeholders: %...% in Headcount's text, the score formula and statuses.

included | placeholderapi | none included:       Headcount's own %headcount_...% placeholders only (docs/placeholders.md lists them). placeholderapi: those plus every PlaceholderAPI placeholder, and %headcount_...% for other plugins. none:           no %...% placeholders at all, Headcount's own included (they show as written).
Register the %headcount_...% expansion so other plugins (scoreboards, tab, chat) can show Headcount's data.

included | luckperms | vault | none included:  Headcount gives permission nodes itself (saved, and re-applied on every join). It can't do groups, tracks, prefixes or suffixes: those actions are skipped with a warning. Use luckperms or vault. luckperms: everything, with LuckPerms' own expiry on timed changes. vault:     through Vault's permission API (groups, prefixes and suffixes need a Vault chat plugin). none:      every permission action is skipped.
Give timed changes LuckPerms' own expiry too, so they end even if Headcount is removed.
Optional "server" context for nodes Headcount adds (empty = global).
Moderation: the ban, mute, kick, warn and jail actions.

included | litebans | libertybans | advancedban | essentials | commands | none included:    vanilla bans (the server's ban list), kicks, warnings (a message), and Headcount's own mute and jail (settings below). commands:    any moderation plugin, driven by the command templates under 'commands'. none:        every moderation action is skipped. A plugin that can't do one kind (LibertyBans and LiteBans have no jail) leaves that kind to 'included'.
Give single kinds their own provider (same choices), e.g. bans by LibertyBans but jail by EssentialsX: kinds: jail: essentials Kinds: ban, mute, kick, warn, jail. Leave out a kind to use 'provider'.

Statuses that stop a request being sent (checked on both players). Messages: gates.trade-send.<status> (you) and gates.trade-send-target.<status> (the other player). Bypass: headcount.bypass.trade-send.<status>.
Statuses that stop a request being accepted (checked on both players). Messages: gates.trade-accept.<status> / gates.trade-accept-target.<status>.
Statuses that cancel an open trade (checked on both players, every cancel.check-interval). Bypass: headcount.bypass.trade-cancel.<status>.

An open trade is cancelled (everything returned to its owner) if either player closes the screen, disconnects, is kicked or banned, dies, changes world, leaves range, gets a cancel status, the cycle ends, or the server stops or reloads. These add more cases:
Teleports shorter than this (in the same world) do not cancel.

options.help: The formula. Normal math: + - * / % (remainder) ^ (power), parentheses, comparisons (< <= > >= == !=, which give 1 or 0), && || !, and "condition ? a : b". Functions: min(a, b, ...) max(...) avg(...) floor ceil round(x[, digits]) trunc abs sign pow(x, y) sqrt cbrt exp log(x[, base]) ln log10 log2 clamp(x, low, high) if(condition, a, b) sin cos tan Constants: pi e true false Variables: unique            unique heads in the vault (different owners; your own head counts once) total             total heads in the vault, duplicates included own               copies of your own head in the vault duplicates        total - unique vault_size        your vault slots this cycle;  vault_free  empty slots starting_heads    heads every vault started with this cycle active            active players this cycle;  players  everyone who has ever joined;  online  players online rank              your rank among active players by unique heads (1 = most; ties share a rank) percentile        your percentile among active players (100 = top, 0 = bottom) unique_avg unique_median unique_max unique_min unique_sum   over active players kills             kill heads you got this cycle;  deaths  kill heads others got from you trades            completed trades;  heads_in / heads_out  heads received / given through trades purchases         shop purchases this cycle;  points_spent  points spent this cycle points            points you hold now;  points_next  points already waiting for next cycle playtime          minutes played this cycle;  playtime_hours streak            +N for N positive cycles in a row, -N for N negative;  streak_positive / streak_negative last_score        last cycle's score (0 if none);  last_unique;  has_last  1 if there was a last score bonus             score bonus from actions (added after the formula unless add-bonus-after-formula is false) titles            titles you own cycle             the cycle ID;  cycle_length  days;  days_elapsed / days_left is_active         1 if you are active %any_placeholder% any numeric PlaceholderAPI placeholder, e.g. %statistic_player_kills% (offline players resolve whatever the placeholder supports; anything non-numeric counts as 0) Default: one point per unique head, minus a quarter of the active players (rounded up). With 12 active players, 3 unique heads scores 0 and 10 unique heads scores 7.

Other ideas (copy one into 'formula'): Exponential, rewarding big collections:   floor(pow(unique, 1.5) / 2) - ceil(active / 4) Percent-based, compared to everyone:      round((percentile - 50) / 10) Rank-based, top 3 rewarded:               rank <= 3 ? 10 - rank * 2 : (percentile < 25 ? -3 : 0) Share of all active players collected:    round(unique / max(active, 1) * 10) - 5 Streak bonus on top of the default:       unique - ceil(active / 4) + min(streak_positive, 3) Punish hoarding your own head:            unique - ceil(active / 4) - floor(own / 10) Kills matter:                             unique + kills - deaths - ceil(active / 4) How the formula's result becomes a whole number: floor | round | ceil
Add the 'score-bonus' action total after the formula and rounding. Set false if your formula uses 'bonus' itself.
How ties rank: competition (10, 10, 8 -> 1, 1, 3) or dense (10, 10, 8 -> 1, 1, 2).
A streak counts consecutive cycles with a positive score, or with a negative score. When a player is inactive for a cycle: pause (keep the streak) | break (reset to 0)
A score of exactly 0: break | pause
all: a player gets every rule their score matches. most-extreme: only the most extreme matching rule in each group (a -12 gets "severe", not all three).
Repeated failure: a ban for three negative cycles in a row. Disabled by default; enable with care.

Entry settings: name                 how the entry is called in messages (default: its display name without formatting) enabled              false hides it page, slot           where it goes (page starts at 1) price                in points display              item definition (material, name, lore, item-model, glint, enchants, custom ...) display-states       per-state overrides (affordable, too-expensive, sold-out, locked, limit-reached, cooldown, unavailable) actions              what a purchase does limit-per-cycle      purchases per player per cycle (0 = no limit) stock                global stock (-1 = unlimited) cooldown             time between purchases per player conditions           extra requirements (see actions.yml) requires             titles: [..], purchases: [entry or tier.entry, ever], purchases-this-cycle: [..], permissions: [..] confirm              force the confirmation menu on (true) or off (false)

recipes.title: A weekly cycle that ends Sunday evening
yaml:
# config.yml
cycle:
  length-days: 7
  start-date: 2026-11-15      # a Sunday
  end-time: "20:00"
  time-zone: America/Denver

recipes.title: Hardcore: harsh punishments and bans for repeat offenders
yaml:
# outcomes.yml
mode: all                      # every matching rule applies
rules:
  ban-repeat-offenders:
    enabled: true
# actions.yml: make punish-mild stronger
  punish-mild:
    - message: "<red>Score <score>. You are slowed for a full day."
    - type: potion
      effect: slowness
      amplifier: 1
      duration: 1d

recipes.title: Points carry over, and big collections are rewarded more
yaml:
# config.yml
points:
  rollover-percent: 50
# scoring.yml
formula: "floor(pow(unique, 1.5) / 2) - ceil(active / 4)"

recipes.title: Using another combat plugin through PlaceholderAPI
yaml:
# statuses.yml
  combat-tagged:
    source: placeholder
    placeholder: "%combatlogx_in_combat%"
    operator: equals
    value: "Yes"
    fallback: recent-pvp-damage

recipes.title: Only count players who actually play
Another scoreboard plugin shows Headcount instead
recipes.text: Then use `%headcount_unique%`, `%headcount_score%`, `%headcount_points%`, `%headcount_time_left%` and `%headcount_streak_text%` in that plugin.

recipes.title: Titles as LuckPerms prefixes
yaml:
# titles.yml
settings:
  permission-prefix:
    enabled: true
    type: prefix
    priority: 100

recipes.title: A shop entry that rents a rank for three days
yaml:
# shop.yml, under a tier's entries
      vip-rental:
        slot: 22
        price: 30
        limit-per-cycle: 1
        display: { material: GOLD_INGOT, name: "<gold>VIP for 3 days" }
        actions:
          - type: group
            group: vip
            duration: 3d
            start-message: "<gold>You are VIP for <duration>."
            end-message: "<gray>Your VIP rental ended."

recipes.title: A punishment that locks PvP on
yaml:
# actions.yml
  punish-pvp:
    - type: pvp
      state: on
      lock: true
      duration: 1d
      start-message: "<red>Your PvP is forced on for a day."

recipes.title: PvP always on in the Nether, and logging out of a fight costs points
yaml:
# integrations.yml
pvp:
  included:
    toggle:
      force-on-worlds: [world_nether]
    combat-log:
      actions:
        - type: points
          amount: -5
        - message: "<red>You logged out during a fight and lost 5 points."

recipes.title: Everyone fights by default, with a longer combat tag
recipes.text: With PvP on by default, the default vault and trade rules (blocked while `in-pvp`) apply to everyone until they turn it off. Remove `in-pvp` from `vault.block-movement.statuses` and the trade statuses if you don't want that.
yaml:
# integrations.yml
pvp:
  included:
    toggle:
      default: "on"
    combat-tag:
      duration: 30s
      block-elytra: true
      block-ender-pearls: true
    messages:
      countdown: bossbar

recipes.title: Bans by LibertyBans, jail by EssentialsX
yaml:
# integrations.yml
moderation:
  provider: libertybans
  kinds:
    jail: essentials

recipes.title: Time zone as an abbreviation or offset
recipes.text: Abbreviations and offsets are fixed: `MST` is UTC-7 all year. A region such as `America/Denver` follows daylight saving.
yaml:
# config.yml
cycle:
  time-zone: MST        # or GMT-7, UTC+5:30, America/Denver, system
